title: Etsy faces backlash over including AI model training in new policy update
summary: Some Etsy sellers across Canada are removing products from the platform amid criticism for introducing AI model training as part of a policy change.

image.caption: This Jan. 6, 2015, file photo shows an Etsy mobile credit card reader, in New York. The online company is facing criticism after introducing AI model training in a recent policy change. ((AP Photo/Mark Lennihan, File))

blocks.text: British Columbia·New
Some Etsy sellers across Canada are removing products from the platform amid criticism for introducing AI model training as part of a policy change.
Vancouver-based seller says the policy 'felt like a kick in the teeth'
Some Etsy sellers across Canada are removing products from the platform amid criticism for introducing artificial intelligence model training as part of a policy change.
Tsuki Matsuba, in Vancouver, B.C., is pulling her custom stationery products from Etsy ahead of a new AI policy the company is rolling out next month.
"It felt like a kick in the teeth," said Matsuba.

There is a line of language within an update to the company’s terms and agreements rolling out Dec. 16 that says Etsy, its third party partners and vendors can use sellers' content to "develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies."

One of the largest accounting and consulting firms in the world, KPMG, reported in 2025 that 88 per cent of tech executives surveyed believe tech companies that embrace AI will develop a competitive edge over those who don't.
It also showed 68 per cent of respondents expect a moderate to very high return on investment related to AI investments — 10 per cent of more.
Canadian backlash
After seven years working in animation, Matsuba said AI was one of the major factors in losing her job in that industry.
She fears shop owners on Etsy are "being forced" to choose between earning holiday income and remaining on the platform under terms that allow their content to be used for AI training.

blocks.text: More Etsy shop owners across Canada are removing products and original artwork from the platform due to concerns that their work will be used to train AI.
Artist Tina Nawrocki, in Ottawa, wrote on X that she is "closing down" her Etsy shop due to the company’s "new predatory AI practices."
Halifax-based artist, The Calendork, announced it has removed all artwork from its Etsy shop while remaining open due to the "new insane AI policies."
'Should have done more'
Etsy’s head of customer operations, James Ossman, said in a statement that respecting its sellers’ work is "central" to the way Etsy runs its business.
He said sellers’ "creative work belongs to them," and Etsy doesn’t use that work to train "AI models designed to copy their original work or replace their creativity."
Etsy to ban the sale of fur, with some Indigenous artists affected most
The company plans to continue discussing the policy change with sellers to "clarify what we mean and our intent in the Terms," said Ossman.
He also said that the company "should have done more" to communicate changes coming with Etsy’s updated policies with the platform’s sellers.
But for Matsuba, those discussions won’t change her decision to stop selling her products on the platform.
"My business is completely AI free," she said, "I don’t want to participate in developing AI further."
